title: Multilingual, code-switched and cross-scope roll-up demonstration
purpose: Exercise the post-fix synthesis pipeline (deterministic sampling, verify-and-retry, adaptive budget, user-memory write path, concept graph) against (a) a multilingual synthesis matrix, (b) code-switched single messages, (c) cross-message knowledge consolidation inside one channel, and (d) cross-channel knowledge that should surface the same concepts in separate, isolated scopes.

multilingual_matrix.note: Same business situation expressed natively in twelve languages spanning four script families. The recap must come back in the SAME language as the session. Latin-script languages (English/French/German/Spanish/Vietnamese/Indonesian/Malay/Tagalog) are expected to synthesise cleanly on the Qwen3.5-2B Q4_K_M model; the non-Latin scripts are the stress cases — CJK and Thai are spaceless (no word boundaries) and Arabic is right-to-left. Vietnamese additionally stresses heavy Latin diacritics. Malay (ms) and Tagalog (tl) broaden the SEA coverage the project README claims; they have NO recorded model output in results/rollup_results.json yet, so the public leaderboard lists them as 'pending' until a live `run_rollup.py` run records their recaps.

code_switched.note: Real SME chat threads mix languages within a single message (English technical terms inside a non-English sentence, or two languages in one breath). Each item is one ingested message.
messages: Le client BonjourBio demande un rollback du dernier deploy — the checkout API returns 500 on SEPA payments since 14h.
@priya 確認お願いします: the Postgres read-replica lag is 8 seconds, だから reports are stale right now.
Confirmado con el cliente: el bug solo afecta a pagos con tarjeta 3DS; vamos a hotfix the validation regex y desplegar hoy.
Update: hotfix deployed, latency back to normal. 顧客对応 done, ticket OPS-4471 closed; follow-up: add a regression test für 3DS.

cross_message_rollup.note: Six messages inside ONE channel. Three of them restate the SAME decision (move billing to Postgres) in different words; the rest add an open question, a task and a budget sign-off. A useful system consolidates the repeated decision into a single reinforced recap rather than echoing six lines.

messages.body: Decision: we will migrate the billing database to Postgres next sprint. Owner: Priya.
Quick note from standup — the billing DB move to Postgres is locked in for next sprint, Priya leading.
Re: database — yes, Postgres is the call for billing; Priya owns the cutover, targeting next sprint.
Open question: do we need a read replica before the Postgres cutover to avoid report downtime?
Task: Priya to draft the Postgres migration runbook by Wednesday.
FYI the finance team signed off on the Postgres migration budget today.

cross_message_rollup.expected_consolidation: A single recap naming the Postgres billing migration; the memory should be marked Reinforced because the decision was repeated across messages.

cross_channel_rollup.note: The SAME underlying knowledge (the Postgres billing migration) shows up in three separate, cryptographically-isolated channels seen by different teams. We write user-memory observations into each scope and read each scope's concept graph. Isolation must hold (no scope sees another's rows), yet the shared business concepts should independently surface in each channel's graph — that is cross-channel 'roll-up' under a zero-trust isolation model.
